21 hours in 90 seconds👨🏽‍🌾 ⚠️Flash Warning⚠️ This house was bought near the end of 2025 and the garden was a right state!  I was called in to replace the fence panels and totally rip out the garden  (not the posts, they are a bit crooked but they are still standing😅)  I started with the fence panels, then began to totally clear the area of weeds and any other debris in the garden.  We added 2 railway sleepers at the back for a little flower bed. Then a thick layer of top soil was spread and we rolled out the turf. Then we moved 4 tonnes of hardcore to the back through the house!  Backbreaking stuff.  Thanks to my pal @Wagwarn Abel for jumping on and giving me a hand 🙏 This is obviously unfinished but I think the owner was going to slab the rest himself, so our job is done here for now! As always I wanna know what would YOU do now? There's a bed at the back that's totally empty!  I read and appreciate any comments and genuinely like reading your suggestions🙏 Thanks so much for watching anyway, follow if you haven't already for more vids like this!! 💧🌿 The Backyard Water Feature That Feels Like a Luxury Spa 🌿💧 This circular rain curtain fountain is one of the most calming and visually stunning backyard ideas you can add to an outdoor space. ✨ Modern. Peaceful. Architectural. It turns an ordinary garden into a relaxing sanctuary.  💦 Why This Design Is So Mesmerizing The flowing water creates: ✔️ Continuous soothing sound ✔️ Cooling effect in hot weather ✔️ Movement and reflection ✔️ A dramatic focal point ✔️ Instant spa-like atmosphere The circular shape makes it feel artistic and futuristic while still blending beautifully with nature.  🪵 The Warm Wood + Water Combination The natural wood tones soften the sleek modern design and make the feature feel organic instead of industrial. Paired with: 🌿 Tropical plants 🪨 Black river stones 🌱 Layered greenery 💧 Reflective water surfaces …it creates a luxurious resort vibe right at home.  🧘 A Space Designed for Relaxation Imagine sitting nearby with: ☕ Morning coffee 📖 A book 🎶 Soft music 🌙 Evening lighting 🌧️ The sound of falling water This is the kind of feature that lowers stress the moment you walk outside.  ✨ Why Water Features Transform Gardens Water adds: 💧 Sound 💧 Motion 💧 Reflection 💧 Cooling energy 💧 Wildlife attraction Even small backyard spaces feel larger and more peaceful when water is incorporated thoughtfully.  🌿 Perfect for Modern Landscape Design This feature fits beautifully into: ✔️ Minimalist gardens ✔️ Zen landscapes ✔️ Contemporary patios ✔️ Tropical backyard themes ✔️ Luxury outdoor living spaces It works especially well with wood decking, gravel, stone, and layered greenery.  🛠️ Could This Be DIY? A simplified version absolutely could be. Typical components include: 🔧 Curved metal or wood frame 🔧 Hidden water reservoir 🔧 Recirculating pump 🔧 Fine-drip irrigation tubing or perforated piping 🔧 Drainage stones and waterproof basin The key is smooth water distribution for the “rain curtain” effect.  🌙 Imagine It at Night… Add: ✨ Warm LED uplighting 💡 Hidden strip lights 🔥 Fire bowls nearby 🪴 Accent plants 🌌 Ambient seating …and this becomes an unforgettable nighttime retreat.  🏡 Outdoor Luxury Isn’t Always Huge Sometimes one beautiful centerpiece changes the entire feeling of a backyard. A thoughtfully designed water feature can make even a modest garden feel: 🌿 Elegant 🌿 Peaceful 🌿 High-end 🌿 Restorative  💬 Would You Add This to Your Backyard? 👇 Tell us: 💧 Would you prefer this with lights or natural only? 🌿 Modern minimalist or lush tropical style? 🪵 Wood finish or black metal frame? ☕ Would this be your morning coffee spot or evening relaxation zone?

✨ Want a stunning, weed-free flower bed? Try this easy "pot-in-pot" landscaping hack to keep your borders looking fresh all year long! 📦 First, lay down cardboard along your path and space out heavy-duty black base pots on top. The cardboard acts as an amazing, natural weed barrier. 💧 Next, pour gravel all around the base pots. This hides the cardboard, holds your base pots securely in place, and provides excellent water drainage. 🪴 Now just drop your decorative plants-still in their own nursery pots-directly into the base pots! You can swap them out in seconds when seasons change or easily lift them inside if a freeze hits. 💡 Pro-tips: Mix up your flower colors, put the taller plants in the back, and always match your plants to the amount of sunlight that wall gets.

Five plants that separate a designed garden from a planted one. Rosemary — most people treat it as a herb. Designers use it as a structural evergreen with silver foliage, late winter bloom, and serious drought tolerance once established. Echinops — steel-blue globe thistle that holds its form into winter. Pollinators love it, it seeds around just enough, and nothing else gives you that texture. White Cloud Nepeta — all the soft billowing habit of catmint, none of the blue. Cleaner in a white or silver palette. Underused because most people don’t know it exists. Mountain Hydrangea (Hydrangea serrata) — more refined than arborescens, lacecap form, better fall color, and it actually performs in part shade without flopping. Blue Mist Fothergilla (Fothergilla gardenii ‘Blue Mist’) — blue-green foliage all season, then flame in fall. Native, compact, and genuinely beautiful.
